game.title: UNDERWATCH
game.pitch:
A teenage skater in a beautiful, already-completely-surveilled suburb slowly
learns to see the machine underneath the town, and discovers that the only way
to stay free of it is to become something it cannot predict.

unclassified.doc:
A job, out loud. The board's words are short and the city's are in its own
register: the city never says you are being chased, it says it is tracking.

The hierarchy, in one table. The brief's ordering is the test
(tests/art-direction.test.ts): a person is never out-inked by anything.

How much each kind of thing weighs, and how long a place remembers it.
The ladder is the design. Going round leaves nothing; a stone in the road is
the lightest thing you can do on purpose; a knocked bin is louder; a hack is
clean at the time and leaves its trace later; a camera doing something odd
is noticed; breaking one is the heaviest thing short of throwing something
at a person. Half-lives are in seconds.
The questions only the tester can answer, each tied to a criterion.
What the level change says out loud, and how loud.

missions.title: SHOOT: THE LOT FROM THE AIR
missions.brief: Somebody wants proof the lot exists. Take the shot at the top of a kicker.
missions.threat: None, until you are seen getting there

missions.title: GET TO: OKONJO CYCLE & BOARD
missions.brief: A parcel for the board shop on Market Street. Get it there.

missions.title: HIT: THREE PLAZA CAMERAS
missions.brief: Blind the plaza. A stone in the lens, or ride past the pole and cut its line.

missions.title: TAG: THE PLAZA LEDGES
missions.brief: Grind all three plaza ledges and leave your mark on each. The cameras are right there.

missions.title: GET TO: NORTHGATE PARADE · UNSEEN
missions.brief: Nobody can know you were there. Rated on how little anything saw.

missions.title: RUN: PARADE TO THE LOT
missions.brief: Four checkpoints, in order, against the clock. The last one counts in the air.

missions.title: LIFT: THE RELAY 12 DRIVE
missions.brief: Take the drive off the loading apron, then get it to the Channel. Lifting it is loud.

missions.title: LOSE THEM, THEN GREENWAY HALL
missions.brief: You were seen at the cinema. Everything is on you. Break the signal, then get to the hall.

missions.title: BIG LINE: THE LOT, ALL OF IT
missions.brief: From the far corner of town: grind the lot's handrail, then air both kickers. Nothing is off limits.

story.title: b-weather
texts: Lovely out, isn't it.
App says clear till evening.

story.title: b-score
texts: Our street went up to 94 this month.
Did it? Must be the new doorbell.

story.title: b-plaza
texts: They put two more cameras on the cinema.
Good. Kids were sitting on the steps.

story.title: b-school
texts: Did you sign the SCHOOL form?
You don't sign it. You're just in it.

story.title: b-pa-before
texts: UNDERWATCH CARE: Bellhaven Commons is a safe space. Thank you for keeping it that way.

story.title: b-burglary
texts: Did you get the alert? Northgate.
A burglary. In the afternoon. On Northgate Lane.

story.title: b-kid
texts: They're saying it was a kid from Ridgeline.
One of the skaters. It had his name and everything.

story.title: b-photo
texts: That's the Araya boy, isn't it. From the alert.
He's always been polite to me.

story.title: b-pa-alert
texts: UNDERWATCH CARE: Northgate residents, a person of interest has been identified. Please remain aware.

story.title: b-carvalho
texts: Ines is back from work. Says she never called anybody.
Then who did?

story.title: b-courier
texts: That courier's been up and down the Lane all day.
Hood up, in this. Poor sod.

story.title: b-brennan
texts: Gerald says he saw the boy himself.
Gerald says a lot of things.

story.title: b-dropin
texts: There's an UNDERWATCH woman at the community centre tonight.
A drop-in. You can ask her things, apparently.

story.title: b-devon-home
texts: They let the Araya boy go. He's home.
His mum was out on the drive for an hour.

story.title: b-relay
texts: Half the cameras in town come through that shed.
Nobody told us. They just turned up.

story.title: b-channel
texts: There's a camera on the apron now. Wasn't there when I was a kid.
Floods, they said.

story.title: b-window
texts: Have you read the thing in Okonjo's window?
The parcel bit. Tell me that isn't true.

story.title: b-window-2
texts: There's a petition going round. Put the number back to 99.
I signed the first one. I'll sign this one too.

story.title: b-review
texts: The app says there's a review. About the Northgate thing.
A review. So it's fine, then.

story.title: b-dropped
texts: Whatever happened with that boy?
Nothing. It's in the past.

story.title: b-bangs
texts: That's the third bang this afternoon.
Kids. Or the bins. Or kids in the bins.

story.title: b-clatter
texts: Something keeps clattering out the front.
The app says it's logged. So that's all right, then.

story.title: b-camera-down
texts: The camera on the corner's gone dark.
They'll have somebody out. They always do.

story.title: b-two-more
texts: Somebody broke the one by the post box.
Now they'll put up two.

story.title: b-doorbell
texts: My doorbell said it was offline for a minute.
Mine said everything was normal. Which is worse?

story.title: match
texts: It wasn't sure of the face. It was sure of the street.
How was it 98.7% sure it was Devon?

story.title: where
texts: UNDERWATCH can. It wrote it down itself.
Can anyone prove where Devon was at 4:41?

story.title: burglary
texts: Nothing was stolen. A parcel moved one door down.
What actually happened on Northgate Lane?

story.title: who
texts: Somebody doing their job in the rain.
Whose face was in the frame?

story.title: system
texts: Nobody. Everybody. One reasonable step at a time.
Who decided any of this?

story.title: The match
story.speaker: self
texts: FACIAL MATCH CONFIRMED. 98.7%. ARAYA, DEVON M. A burglary in Northgate, and Devon was standing right next to me.

story.title: The frame
story.speaker: record
texts: CM-207 caught the frame at 04:41:07. No fault in 411 days. It passed the frame on exactly the way it was built to.

story.title: The face
story.speaker: record
texts: The frame was checked against a gallery that includes 812 Ridgeline kids. Raw similarity to Devon: 61.2%. The face was hooded and half turned away.

story.title: The association
story.speaker: record
texts: Devon's 'Northgate association' is 0.97: forty-one visits to his cousin on Northgate Lane. The match score is the face weighted by that.

story.title: The threshold
story.speaker: record
texts: Review 11-04: a parents' petition lowered the match threshold from 99.0% to 97.0%. False positives went up 340%. "Within tolerance." Approved by P. Venn.

story.title: He was with me
story.speaker: self
texts: Devon was with me in the Channel the whole time. That's my word. My word isn't a record.

story.title: The apron camera
story.speaker: person
texts: Devon: "the camera on the apron. the little light came on when we went down. it saw us."

story.title: The drainage log
story.speaker: record
texts: The drainage camera logged two subjects entering the Channel at 04:39:52: SUBJECT 4417 and ARAYA, DEVON M. It never compared that with anything.

story.title: Reported on her behalf
story.speaker: place
texts: The UNDERWATCH HOME panel by No. 14's door, still lit: 'UNRECOGNISED ADULT REMOVED AN ITEM FROM YOUR PORCH · 04:41. INCIDENT REPORTED ON YOUR BEHALF.'

story.title: Mrs. Carvalho
story.speaker: person
texts: She didn't report anything. She was at work; the app did it. Nothing's missing. Except a parcel she's been waiting on all week.

story.title: The parcel next door
story.speaker: place
texts: On No. 16's step: a parcel addressed to 14 Northgate Lane. A courier's card taped on top: 'Tried 14. Secure address, no porch drops. Left with neighbour.'

story.title: The community alert
story.speaker: place
texts: The bus shelter screen is running an UNDERWATCH CARE alert: Devon's school photo, PERSON OF INTEREST · NORTHGATE. Posted 04:43, to every phone on the Lane.

story.title: An eyewitness
story.speaker: person
texts: Mr. Brennan says he saw 'the Araya boy' outside No. 14. 'Clear as day. I'd know him anywhere.'

story.title: The courier
story.speaker: person
texts: "Had one for 14. Doorbell said secure address, no porch drops, so I picked it back up and left it at 16. Twenty to five? Hood up. It was spitting."

story.title: Where it all goes
story.speaker: person
texts: Mara watched them fit Northgate's cameras. "It all goes out through a cabinet at Relay 12, the haulage yard off East Avenue. Nobody voted on any of it."

story.title: The shed
story.speaker: record
texts: TX-2 carries every frame Northgate takes. No storage, no matching, no decisions. Just carriage: 100% availability, 41 months.

story.title: Provisioning
story.speaker: record
texts: Relay 12 was bought for winter gritting telemetry. Camera segments get added to it without council approval. 'No capacity review scheduled. None required.'

story.title: The staff camera
story.speaker: record
texts: The office camera at Relay 12 runs on a different uplink. Staff are told, can object, and it is deleted after 30 days.

story.title: Everyone at Ridgeline
story.speaker: place
texts: The gallery is the whole school: 812, everyone enrolled, nobody opted out. On the sign, in biro: Kofi Mensah was brought in for a week last spring, and he still doesn't know what for.

story.title: Last April
story.speaker: place
texts: Under the leaflets, an older alert in the same layout as Devon's: PERSON OF INTEREST · COMMONS, last April. Someone scratched the face out. What's left of the name: '…ENSAH'.

story.title: Down here all week
story.speaker: place
texts: Scratched low on the wall under the footbridge: KOFI M, a date last April, and 'down here all week. the little light saw me.'

story.title: Devon's record
story.speaker: record
texts: SVC-RECORD: 'CONTACT 04:52. NO FURTHER ACTION.' Kept indefinitely. Subjects cannot amend it.

story.title: Sure of the street, not the face
texts: The face was a 61% match. The other thirty-seven points came from where Devon usually goes. It didn't recognise him. It recognised Northgate.

story.title: Under the old line
texts: 98.7 clears 97, not 99. Before the petition, this match would never have fired.

story.title: It isn't just my word
texts: If the apron camera saw us go down, then somewhere there's a record of where Devon was. It's on the apron. I just have to go and read it.

story.title: Two places at once
texts: UNDERWATCH logged Devon entering the Channel at 04:39:52. Seventy-five seconds later CM-207 'saw' him on Northgate Lane, across town. Nobody put the two records side by side.

story.title: Nobody called it in
texts: Mrs. Carvalho was at work. No person reported a burglary. The house did, on her behalf.

story.title: A parcel, not a burglary
texts: The 'item removed from the porch' at 04:41 was her own parcel, carried one door down because the house wouldn't let it be left. Nothing was stolen. There was no burglary.

story.title: The face in the hood
texts: The face CM-207 caught was hooded, at twenty to five, outside No. 14. So was the courier. Whoever the frame is of, it was somebody delivering a parcel.

story.title: What Mr. Brennan saw
texts: The alert with Devon's photo went out at 04:43. Mr. Brennan saw the alert, and then he remembered a boy. He never saw Devon.

story.title: Nobody decided
texts: Nobody voted for any of it. A gritting sensor had cameras added to it one segment at a time; a petition moved a threshold two points. Every step was somebody's reasonable idea.

story.title: Who gets to object
texts: The people who work at Relay 12 can object to their own footage, and it's gone in thirty days. Devon can't object to his, and it's kept forever.

story.title: It could have been any of us
texts: Every kid at Ridgeline is in the gallery, and every one of us has somewhere we usually go. Devon's was his cousin's street. Mine is the Channel.

story.title: It's happened before
texts: Last April it was Kofi, on the Commons. He was down here, the apron camera saw him, and nobody read that either. Devon isn't a glitch. He's the second one I know about.

story.title: One cabinet
texts: Every frame from Northgate goes through one cabinet in a haulage yard, which does nothing but pass it along. There is nothing there to switch off, because nothing there decides.

story.title: sl-enrol
texts: 'All Ridgeline pupils are enrolled.' All of them. That's the 812. Under 'opt-out forms', in biro, small enough to miss: 'they had Kofi Mensah in for a week last spring. ask him what for. he doesn't know either.'

story.title: sl-noticeboard
texts: You lift the CARE leaflet. Under it, sun-bleached, the same layout as the shelter screen: PERSON OF INTEREST · COMMONS. Last April. Somebody has scratched the face out with a key, carefully, like they were being kind. What's left of the name: '…ENSAH'.

story.title: sl-ledge
texts: You know the name now, so you find it. Low on the wall, scratched deep: KOFI M. Under it, the same hand, a date from last April, and: 'down here all week. the little light saw me.'

story.title: sl-graffiti
texts: SMILE · YOU'RE PREDICTED. And underneath: not down here. Except it was down here. The apron camera had the two of you at 04:39:52 the whole time. Nobody asked it.

story.title: sl-devon-board
texts: NOT A MATCH, in marker, on the nose of his board. Under it, smaller, like he came back and added it later: 61.

story.title: sl-dropin
texts: 'Meet Priya Venn, your Regional Operations lead. Your questions make us better.' P. Venn. The same name as the bottom of the threshold review. Five o'clock. You have a question.

story.title: sl-alert
texts: Devon's school photo, on a loop. Posted 04:43. You watch it go round twice. Every phone on the Lane got this. Two minutes later, people were remembering a boy.

story.title: sl-doorbell
texts: The green light. 'This home is protected.' So was No. 14. If somebody picks up a parcel on this step while they're at work, the house will report it for them, and by the time they're home it will be true.

story.title: A Second Line
texts: Priya Venn opened a formal review that evening. She read every page of your notes, twice.
INC-4100 was reclassified: no offence, misattribution. Devon's record was not deleted (it can't be), but it has a second line now, under the first.
The match threshold went back to 99% the following quarter. The petition that lowered it wasn't mentioned in the minutes.
Devon still doesn't skate Northgate Lane. But he goes to his cousin's again.

story.title: Your Concern Has Been Logged
texts: Priya Venn listened, and she was kind about it, and she logged it under reference CX-20417.
"Association is not an accusation," she said. You could tell she believed it.
Nothing in Devon's record changed. Nothing in the system needed to. It had worked exactly as designed.
You still have the notes. They were right. They just were not enough.

story.title: The Window
texts: Mara put the whole thing in her window, in marker and printouts: the frame, the face, the drainage log, the parcel.
By the weekend half of Bellhaven had stopped to read it. By the council meeting, 380 people had signed to put the threshold back to 99%.
UNDERWATCH issued community guidance about unverified claims. Your Community Safety Score dropped eleven points and never quite came back.
Devon keeps a photo of the window on his phone. He says it's the only record of him he likes.

story.title: A Kid Defending His Friend
texts: Mara put your notes in her window. People read them the way people read a kid defending a friend.
There were holes in it, and the holes were what got repeated. Mr. Brennan told anyone who'd listen that he'd seen the boy himself.
The notice came down after a week. The community alert stayed up for a month.
Devon stopped coming to the Commons. He said it wasn't your fault. It sort of was.

story.title: Let It Go
texts: You told Devon you would let it go, and you did.
His record says CONTACT 04:52 · NO FURTHER ACTION, and it will say that for the rest of his life, to anyone who's allowed to ask.
He was grateful. He meant it. The two of you never skate Northgate Lane again, and neither of you says why.
The town is very safe. Everyone says so.

A job, out loud. The board's words are short and the city's are in its own

the lightest thing you can do on purpose; a knocked bin is louder; a hack is
clean at the time and leaves its trace later; a camera doing something odd
is noticed; breaking one is the heaviest thing short of throwing something
at a person. Half-lives are in seconds.
